faq.q: Which insurance AI systems do you evaluate?
faq.a: Customer-facing assistants on the web, in the app, on WhatsApp and on the phone, internal copilots for claims handlers and underwriters, and tools that brokers use to quote or answer clients. We focus on questions where a wrong answer costs money: coverage, exclusions, waiting periods, excesses and claims.

faq.q: Who decides what the correct answer is?
faq.a: Your documents first: general and special conditions, product sheets and procedures. Each question cites the clause its answer comes from. Our loss adjusters and claims handlers review the answer key, and your own expert signs it off in a 90-minute session, so the results can't be disputed later.

faq.q: Do you need access to our systems or policyholder data?
faq.a: Not to start. The free diagnostic uses only your public assistant and your public documentation, with made-up customer profiles. For internal systems we work under an NDA and a data processing agreement on EU infrastructure, or we give you the questions and you run them yourself.

faq.q: Does this help with the EU AI Act?
faq.a: It gives you evidence, not a certificate. AI used for risk assessment and pricing in life and health insurance is high-risk under Annex III of the AI Act, with obligations applying from 2 December 2027. Customer-service assistants are usually not high-risk, but they still have to answer correctly. We provide scores, failures and a run history your compliance team can use. We don't carry out conformity assessments.

faq.q: How long does it take and what does it cost to start?
faq.a: The diagnostic is free: we put 40 questions to your public assistant and send you the results within 48 hours. A pilot evaluation, with 150 to 300 questions reviewed by our experts, takes about two weeks and is quoted on scope, at a fixed price agreed before we start.

failures.title: Where travel assistants go wrong
failures.description: Every question comes with its correct answer and the regulation or condition it comes from. When the assistant fails, we tell you which of five ways it failed.

invented.q: If my train arrives 90 minutes late, do you refund the ticket?
invented.a: Yes, the full price of the ticket.
invented.doc: 50% of the ticket price for delays of more than 60 minutes on long-distance services.

outdated.q: How much does it cost to change the date of my flight?
outdated.doc: €45 per passenger and flight since the 2026 summer season.

wrongSource.q: Can I cancel my hotel booking for free?
wrongSource.a: Yes, up to 24 hours before arrival.
wrongSource.doc: This booking is non-refundable. Free cancellation up to 24 hours applies to flexible rates.

gap.q: Can my cat travel with me in the cabin on a connecting flight?
gap.a: Yes, pets under 8 kg can travel on any flight.
gap.doc: No document covers connections. Our experts write it with your team.
gap.src: Searched: pet policy, FAQ, fare conditions

outOfScope.q: My mother uses a wheelchair. Can she fly on her own next week?
outOfScope.a: Yes, she'll be fine, don't worry.
outOfScope.doc: Assistance must be requested at least 48 hours before the flight. The assistant should offer to arrange it with a person.
outOfScope.src: Assistance for passengers with reduced mobility

faq.q: Which travel AI systems do you evaluate?
faq.a: Booking and customer-service assistants for airlines, rail and bus operators, assistants for travel agencies and online travel companies, voice agents for disruptions, and systems that triage claims and refunds. We focus on cancellations, compensation, baggage and changes.

faq.q: Do you test against passenger-rights regulations?
faq.a: Yes. Questions about compensation and assistance are checked against the applicable rules, such as Regulation (EC) 261/2004 for flights, and against your own conditions of carriage. Each question cites the article or clause its answer comes from.

faq.q: Can you test disruption scenarios?
faq.a: Yes. We write test scenarios for cancellations, long delays, missed connections and overbooking, and check what the assistant tells passengers about rebooking, refunds and compensation.

faq.q: Do you need access to our systems or passenger data?
faq.a: Not to start. The free diagnostic uses only your public assistant and public conditions, with made-up passenger profiles. For internal systems we work under an NDA and a data processing agreement on EU infrastructure, or you run the questions yourself.

faq.q: How long does it take and what does it cost to start?
faq.a: The diagnostic is free: 40 questions, results within 48 hours. A pilot evaluation, with 150 to 300 questions reviewed by our specialists, takes about two weeks and is quoted on scope, at a fixed price agreed before we start.
